title: Privacy-Aware Evaluator Sandbox and Probe Curation Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the Privacy-Aware Evaluator Sandbox (PAES): a reproducible, auditable environment for running model evaluations and curating probe sets while preserving customer-sensitive signals and supporting quantization-aware workflows. The target audience is applied-ML engineers, evaluator stewards, and Platform SREs who run shadow evaluations against private or dedicated deployments.

Goals

- Enable high-fidelity evals that mimic production traffic while ensuring privacy controls (redaction, differential privacy, and telemetry bucketing).
- Make probe curation reproducible and traceable: provenance, annotator contracts, retention policy.
- Provide a standard config and gating flow for quantization-sensitive evaluations so decisions about model promotion or fallback are clearly justified.
- Ship an operational runbook for triage, rollback, and artifact retention.

Scope and non-goals

- In scope: shadow traffic sampling, probe seeding and pruning, DP-enabled metrics, quantized-replay validation, provenance metadata capture, and sandbox resource tagging.
- Out of scope: customer-facing incident communication templates (see customer-success-and-support), full production migration steps (see model-onboarding).

High-level architecture

1) Ingress: controlled shadow tap that mirrors a sampled subset of production requests into PAES.
2) Probe Fabricator: generator service (hybrid of synthetic + seeded real examples) that emits labeled probes with provenance IDs.
3) Evaluator Workers: containerized evaluation jobs that run model variants (full-precision and quantized) against probe sets.
4) Privacy Layer: redaction hooks, token-level masking, and DP aggregator for metrics.
5) Artifact Store: immutable evaluation snapshots (prompt families, model binary hashes, config yaml, telemetry digest).
6) Triage Dashboard and Alerting: SLO/quality gates integration with Redwood Console.

Ownership and contacts

- Product owner: Applied ML - Maya Thompson (author)
- Engineering lead: Connor Wu
- Privacy reviewer: Elaine González (Legal & Security liaison)
- Oncall triage: eng-sre team (pager: #sre-evals)

Probe lifecycle (detailed)

1. Seed collection
   - Source: production-sampled requests, annotated anonymized support logs, and synthetic generators.
   - Sampling policy: 1% of requests by default, stratified by tenant size and route. For high-risk routes (PII), use 0.1% and DP aggregation.

2. Curation and labeling
   - Annotator contract (must include): label schema, acceptance criteria, inter-annotator agreement threshold (Krippendorff alpha >= 0.7), retention TTL.
   - All probes get provenance_id: PAES-YYYYMMDD-<generator>-<sha1>.

3. Privacy transformation
   - Redaction rules applied in-flight using the redaction pipeline: email, ssn, credit_card, name entities. Rules maintained in: /configs/eval-redaction-registry.yaml.
   - Apply token-level bucketing before retention for analysis.

4. Probe promotion and TTL
   - Fresh probes promoted after passing annotation QA; archived after 180 days unless explicitly flagged for retention.

Quantization-aware evaluation protocol

When evaluating a quantized candidate, follow these steps exactly:

1) Baseline run (FP16 or FP32) on the same probe set to collect reference metrics.
2) Quantized run (target quant profile) with identical RNG seeds and prompt normalization.
3) Replay alignment: use the quantized-replay harness to capture token-level divergences and KV-cache behavior.

Config table (required fields for an evaluation job)

| field | description | example |
|------|-------------|--------|
| job_id | stable evaluation job id | paes-job-20260210-07 |
| model_hash | content-addressed model binary identifier | sha256:abc123... |
| quant_profile | quant strategy used | int8-llm-qs16 |
| probe_manifest | path to probe bundle in artifact store | s3://paes/artifacts/probe-manifests/20260210.json |
| dp_budget | epsilon,delta for DP aggregation | 1.0,1e-5 |
| retention_ttl_days | probe retention policy | 180 |
| owner | team or person accountable | applied-ml/maya-thompson |

(Represent the table above as plain text in Confluence)

Example job config (YAML)

```
job_id: paes-job-20260210-07
model_hash: sha256:abc123def4567890
quant_profile: int8-llm-qs16
probe_manifest: s3://paes/artifacts/probe-manifests/20260210.json
dp_budget:
  epsilon: 1.0
  delta: 1e-5
retention_ttl_days: 180
owner: applied-ml/maya-thompson
```

Privacy controls and DP guidance

- Default DP settings for public-facing routes: epsilon <= 1.0, delta <= 1e-5. For internal-only evaluations use epsilon up to 2.5 with documented approval from Privacy reviewer.
- Metrics must be aggregated using the DP aggregator library (see evaluator-sidecar contract). Raw prompts must never be stored unredacted unless approved and with HSM-backed access controls.
- Telemetry retention: scrubbed telemetry buckets kept for 365 days; full-text probes adhere to retention_ttl_days.

Acceptance criteria and quality gates

Numeric acceptance criteria for promotion to canary: all must be satisfied
- Coherence delta (quantized vs baseline) <= 1.2% on human-anchored coherence metric
- Latency P95 (quantized) <= baseline P95 * 1.35
- Safety sentinel false_positive_delta <= 0.05 absolute
- Embedding drift (cosine) <= 0.03 mean difference

If any gate fails, follow the triage playbook below.

Triage and rollback playbook (operational steps)

1. On alert: capture evaluation job_id, model_hash, quant_profile, and probe_manifest.
2. Reproduce locally with the small-probe-sample (1000 probes) using `paes-run --job <job_id> --sample 1000`.
3. If behavior is reproducible, escalate to applied-ml owner and open a regression issue with labeled artifacts.
4. If not reproducible, check telemetry: RNG seed drift, redaction differences, and hardware affinity mismatches.
5. Rollback criteria: if safety sentinel failure or coherence delta > 3x acceptance threshold, block promotion and revert any canary routing.

Operational commands and examples

- Start a sandbox evaluation (CLI):

```
paes-run --job paes-job-20260210-07 --env sandbox --trace --dp-budget 1.0
```

- Generate a probe manifest from sampled traffic:

```
paes-probe-fab --source mirror-stream --sample-rate 0.01 --out s3://paes/artifacts/probe-manifests/20260210.json
```

Monitoring and alerting

- Dashboards: PAES Quality Overview (per-model, per-quant-profile), Probe Age Distribution, DP Budget Consumption.
- Alerts: quality-gate-failure (severity P1), DP-budget-exhausted (severity P2), artifact-store-mismatch (severity P2).
- Pager assignment: first responder is the Applied ML oncall, then eng-sre after 15 minutes.

Audit and provenance

- Every evaluation produces an immutable artifact bundle: {job_id, model_hash, quant_profile, probe_manifest, dp_budget, run_metadata}. Bundles are hashed and stored in artifact-store with lifecycle policies.
- Manual review checkpoints require two approvers for restricted probes (sensitive customers) and one approver for general probes.

Onboarding checklist for a new evaluator steward

1. Read this playbook and complete privacy training.
2. Get S3 write access to paes artifact bucket (request through infra).
3. Complete hands-on run: execute a baseline run and a quantized run using the sample manifest.
4. Demonstrate ability to interpret DP-aggregated metrics and trace token divergence.
5. Request approval to run restricted-route probes if needed.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations

- Mode: KV-cache divergence between FP baseline and quantized run. Mitigation: enable cache-aligned replay, capture KV-diffs, and re-run with warmed cache.
- Mode: DP budget breach during a long sweep. Mitigation: reduce sample rate, increase bucketing granularity, or request privacy escalation with approval.
- Mode: Annotator drift post-relabel. Mitigation: run adjudication, refresh inter-annotator agreement measures, and freeze slice for retraining.
